title: The CAP Theorem: Brewer's 2000 Conjecture, Proved in 2002
explainer: Eric Brewer presented the idea as a conjecture at the 2000 Symposium on Principles of Distributed Computing: a distributed data store can give at most two of consistency, availability, and partition tolerance at once. In 2002, MIT researchers Seth Gilbert and Nancy Lynch published a formal proof, turning Brewer's conjecture into the CAP theorem. Every cloud architecture decision about multi-region databases, eventual consistency, or failover behavior is, underneath, a choice about which two of those three guarantees to keep during a network partition.

title: Little's Law (1961) and Capacity Planning
explainer: In 1961, John Little published a rigorous proof of what is now called Little's Law: in a stable queueing system, the average number of items in the system (L) equals the arrival rate (lambda) multiplied by the average time each item spends in the system (W), or L = lambda * W. This simple relationship underlies cloud capacity planning: it lets engineers reason about how request rate, concurrency limits, and latency targets constrain each other when sizing autoscaling groups or connection pools.
